note: The GLOBAL level of the presentation cascade — this instance's default rendition for each token family the app can show more than one way. 'wired' is the app's rendition (a checkbox you can click, an <h3>, a rendered sentence, a tag as a chip); 'raw' is the characters, verbatim. GLOBAL is the LEAST specific of the seven levels, so anything a more specific level says beats it — in particular the cursor: put the cursor on a line and it shows its source characters whatever this file says. A key left out of this file stays silent and falls through to the built-in default; a key MISSPELLED here is reported as a problem rather than ignored, because a declaration nobody reads is the bug this level exists to disprove. 'tags' is the one key whose built-in default is 'raw' and whose value here is 'wired': the floor is what the app did before the key existed, and the chip is a decision this INSTANCE makes. Flip it to 'raw', or delete it, and the chips become characters with nothing rebuilt. Served with the app from the site root and read by app/present/declaration.ts. See docs/implementation-artifacts/design-presentation-cascade.md.
